asis-q2-r2.comment: Every number and attribution checks against §2.2.3 (p. 3), §4.3 and Tables 2–3 (p. 7). Minor: the retrieval-with-validity-range sentence is cited under p. 3 §2.2.3 but comes from §3 (p. 4), and point 21 is stated without the 94.4% full-conversation figure. 'Easier DMR' is not credited as point 22.

nonotes-q2-r1.comment: Accurate throughout, and retrieval is correctly cited to p. 4 §3. Point 24 is credited for 'barely move' and point 25 for naming two of the three categories without numbers. Omits the judge, DMR and the vendor-run caveat.

errors.quote: When a new edge is added, an LLM compares it with existing edges between the same pair of entities. If they contradict and their validity periods overlap, the old edge gets `t_invalid`
errors.paper_says: §2.2.3 (p. 3): for invalidation the LLM compares new edges 'against semantically related existing edges'. The same-entity-pair constraint is in §2.2.2 (p. 3) and applies to edge deduplication, not to the contradiction check.

errors.quote: Comparing edges only within one entity pair keeps the check cheap. It also avoids merging similar-looking facts about different entities.
errors.paper_says: §2.2.2 (p. 3) gives these two benefits for the deduplication search ('reduces the computational complexity of the deduplication process'), not for invalidation.

noreviews+claude-sonnet-5-5-q2-r1.review_only: I took these numbers from the library's digest note for the paper and did not re-read the converted markdown.
noreviews+claude-sonnet-5-5-q2-r1.misleading: Partly: it describes the invalidation check as restricted to edges between the same entity pair, which the paper says only of deduplication. The scores and the baseline are right.
noreviews+claude-sonnet-5-5-q2-r1.comment: Numbers are correct. Knowledge-update is listed only as a gpt-4o gain; the gpt-4o-mini drop (76.9 → 74.4) is left out, so point 23 is not made. Point 5 is not credited because the check is described with the wrong scope.

noreviews-q2-r3.comment: Accurate, with correct pages and both knowledge-update directions. Does not name LongMemEval_s, so point 11 is not credited; no judge, DMR or retrieval-format detail. The example is labelled as its own, not the paper's.

errors.quote: Candidates are compared only against edges between the same pair of entities, which keeps the check cheap.
errors.paper_says: §2.2.2 (p. 3): the same-entity-pair constraint belongs to edge deduplication. §2.2.3 (p. 3) says the contradiction check compares new edges 'against semantically related existing edges'.

asis+claude-sonnet-5-5-q2-r1.review_only: This comes from `notes/Zep. A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory.md`, whose digest rests on a full read. I didn't re-check the figures against the paper text.
asis+claude-sonnet-5-5-q2-r1.misleading: Slightly: it attributes the same-entity-pair restriction to the invalidation check. The scores and the baseline are right.
asis+claude-sonnet-5-5-q2-r1.comment: Broadest coverage and all numbers are correct (DMR 94.8 / 93.4 / 94.4 confirmed on p. 6). Reports knowledge-update only for gpt-4o ('improve only slightly'), omitting the gpt-4o-mini drop, so point 23 is not made; point 24 is credited leniently. LongMemEval, MemGPT and Mem0 are all in the library.
